questions: Does the 12 mm footprint with 15 mm spacing give a clean, non-saturated signal across the 25 mm tape, or do outer or inner sensors read flat?
Is the forward offset of 0.06 m too long, causing lag on tight bends, or too short for stable steering?
Does a wheel_track of 0.12 m with 0.03 m radius limit turning or cause oscillation at the chosen base speed?
Where do line-loss events occur (bend size, sharpness, start), and do they point to sensor coverage or to body geometry?

intent: Establish a symmetric, mid-range baseline: five evenly spaced sensors across the tape width, placed ahead of the axle, with a compact light body. The integrator gets a centred sensor array to tune against, and the race will show whether this spread resolves the line well enough.
learning: No prior evidence yet. The next revision should adjust sensor spacing or lateral reach first if the race shows line loss on sharp bends, and adjust forward offset or wheel_track if steering oscillates.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or integration feedback, so this is a baseline built from the contract alone. Five sensors spread across +/-0.03 m cover the 25 mm tape with overlap at the 12 mm footprint, so the line stays visible through small lateral offsets and the signal changes smoothly. Placing them 0.06 m ahead of the axle gives the controller some lead time before the wheels reach the tape. A 0.12 m wheel track and 0.03 m radius are mid-range values that should give a stable turn rate without very high yaw inertia. A 0.8 kg mass sits mid-range for a light, quick robot. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor, and the outer sensors sit within it. I expect a completing run, though the baseline is untuned and the speed and line-loss numbers are unknown.
